source_title: Celine Dion's former Florida mansion sells for $12.5m after $20m listing
source_excerpt: A waterfront mansion in Jupiter, Florida, once built for Canadian singer Celine Dion, has been sold for $12.5 million in an off-market deal. The sprawling Mediterranean-style property, located in the exclusive Admirals Cove community, was originally designed and built for the Grammy-winning singer in 1998.The sale marks a significant real estate transaction for the luxury housing market in South Florida. The 14,750-square-foot mansion was previously listed for $20 million in May before being taken off the market in August, according to The Real Deal.Local investor Myron Miller purchased the property at 370 Eagle Drive for approximately $847 per square foot. The seller was an entity linked to Edward St. John, the founder and chairman of Baltimore-based St. John Properties.Celine Dion owned the mansion until 2002The waterfront residence was built for Celine Dion in 1998, reflecting a Mediterranean architectural style with expansive interiors and luxury amenities. The singer owned the property until 2002, when she sold it for $9 million, according to property records.The mansion later changed hands in June 2021, when an entity linked to St. John acquired it for $7.6 million. The latest $12.5 million transaction represents an increase of approximately 64 per cent over the 2021 purchase price.Although the property was marketed for $20 million earlier this year, the final transaction was completed off-market. The residence was sold furnished and offers extensive indoor and outdoor amenities, along with views of the waterfront.The primary suite features a stone fireplace, a spacious sitting area and access to a terrace. Other highlights include a private home theatre with red velvet seats, a coffered ceiling and a crystal chandelier, as well as a wine cellar.The outdoor spaces include a covered patio with an outdoor kitchen, a swimming pool and a hot tub overlooking the water. The property also comes with a private dock, offering access to the waterways and the ocean.The mansion is located within Admirals Cove, a gated luxury community known for its country club, golf course, restaurants, swimming pools and water access.Why the buyer chose the exclusive Admirals Cove communityAccording to buyerâs agent Willie Abreu of the Nicolas Group at Serhant, the communityâs lifestyle offerings played a significant role in the purchase.âMy buyer is huge into golf and has kids, so he loves that the community is gated, and heâs able to get everywhere on a golf cart,â Abreu said, according to Mansion Global. He also highlighted the communityâs amenities, including its gym, restaurants and pools, describing the experience as âbasically resort livingâ.The property's waterfront location and private dock were additional attractions for Miller, who is an investor and an avid golfer.Thomson has also described Admirals Cove as a community with such extensive amenities that it feels like a âDisney for adultsâ. The neighbourhood has attracted several high-profile residents over the years, including Donald Trump Jr., professional golfer Dustin Johnson and Major League Baseball star Max Scherzer.Jupiterâs luxury real estate market attracts wealthy buyersThe recent sale occurs in the context of ongoing growth within Jupiterâs luxury real estate sector, where properties situated along the waterfront and residences within exclusive gated communities are experiencing a significant surge in demand, particularly among wealthy buyers who are looking for premium options.In Admirals Cove, there has been an observable trend of high-value real estate transactions taking place over the past few months.
